content.title: About
content.content: Chicken fillet wrap sandwich, fried is a fast‑food item consisting of a breaded chicken fillet wrapped in a thin tortilla and deep‑fried. The sandwich combines a crispy exterior, juicy meat and fresh vegetables, often served with a sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish appeared in the early 2000s as a lighter fast‑food alternative.
The chicken fillet is usually marinated in spices and breaded before frying.
The wrap can be made from wheat, whole‑grain or gluten‑free flour.
Some locations add avocado or cheddar cheese for extra flavor.
It is commonly served with french fries and a soft drink.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken fillet provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Lower fat than beef
items.content: Chicken contains less saturated fat than red meat, making it a more heart‑friendly option.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat supplies niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It provides phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bones and immunity.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The wrap’s carbohydrates give a quick boost of energy.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Sauces and seasonings can raise the salt level, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Trans fats in breading
items.content: Deep‑frying can create trans fats that are detrimental to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The sandwich can be high in calories due to oil and bread, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is hand‑held; you can add fresh lettuce, tomatoes or extra sauce to taste. For a lighter version, choose a whole‑grain wrap and limit the amount of sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared sandwich in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, keep the components separate and assemble just before serving.
